lens: Owner and access-sensitive user; ambiguous result (simulated AI panel seat)
reason: The public desktop/mobile heroes communicate a coherent, legible Precision Instrument identity and a clear student-led consulting proposition. I traced Home to Join to Apply through source, including materials and review disclosures: original resumes can identify applicants, and the copy now says so. Owner incident access is restricted by cycle/current role in SQL, uncertain new-account writes preserve access, and resolution explicitly records remediation without repairing accounts. However, ambiguous outcomes remain poorly handled in the actual add-person journey. This prevents unqualified acceptance for this access-sensitive task. This is source/capture and supplied local-test evidence, not observed user success or hosted integration acceptance.

findings.evidence: useRushAction resets the form and refreshes for every response.ok without reading a success receipt (78-80); a thrown fetch becomes only “Request failed” (81-83). PeopleControls uses this for both account creation and existing-account access (162,166). Unlike ResolveButton, it neither validates acknowledgement nor explains uncertain completion.
findings.userImpact: A lost response after a committed account/membership write looks like failure and invites retry. A malformed successful response clears the entered details without confirming the intended operation.
findings.suggestedFix: Require an action-specific receipt before resetting. Preserve form details on uncertain responses and explicitly direct the owner to inspect People, Clerk and account incidents before retrying. Add focused lost-response and malformed-receipt checks for the actual PeopleControls flow.

findings.evidence: ADD_EXISTING_USER links identity and grants membership without the incident recording/transport classification used by ADD_USER. An identity RPC error becomes a generic 409 at 166; the grant at 167 falls through to generic action error handling, and thrown RPC failures escape this branch.
findings.userImpact: The existing-account operation owners use to finish partial provisioning can itself have an uncertain commit without creating a recovery-queue entry or giving phase-specific reconciliation guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply restricted incident recording and bounded uncertain-outcome responses to existing-account identity/grant failures too; preserve existing access and test acknowledgement loss after each write.

notVerified: No staging or hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration exists in the evidence; current-role/session-expiry behavior and provider compensation were not exercised end to end.

The eight passing privacy browser checks use an intercepted synthetic resolution-button harness; they do not demonstrate actual owner queue loading, account lookup, repair or the complete add-person journey.

No authenticated owner-queue capture, human usability study, assistive-technology session, physical-device or Safari/Firefox evidence was available. Source review does not establish privacy comprehension or successful recovery.
Retention policy and Board approval of original-resume access remain external decisions; client-approved project artifacts/results remain absent.
